questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the film started before I arrived.
questions.q: When I arrived, the film ___ started.

questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the missed breakfast happened before she felt hungry.
questions.q: She was hungry because she ___ breakfast.

questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the earlier of two past events.
questions.q: I recognised him because I ___ him before.

questions.explanation: 'By the time' with a past moment takes the past perfect.
questions.q: By the time we got home, they ___ dinner.

questions.explanation: The past perfect with 'already' shows the concert finished before we arrived.
questions.q: When we arrived, the concert ___.

questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the lack of experience before that past moment.
questions.q: I was nervous because I ___ never ___ on a plane before.

questions.explanation: Past perfect = had + past participle: 'had gone'.
options: She has gone home early yesterday.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?

questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the lack of study happened before the exam.
questions.q: He failed the exam because he ___.

questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the keys were lost before she reached the door.
questions.q: She couldn't open the door because she ___ her keys.

questions.explanation: The past perfect with 'already' shows he left before I arrived.
questions.q: When I got to the office, my boss ___.

questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the haircut happened before the meeting.
questions.q: I didn't recognise her because she ___ her hair.

questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous shows the work continued up to that past moment.
questions.q: They were exhausted because they ___ since dawn.

questions.explanation: Past perfect for the earlier action, past simple for the later one.
options: After the film had finished, we went home.
After the film has finished, we went home.
After the film finished, we had gone home.
After the film had finished, we had gone home.
questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?

questions.explanation: Past perfect = had + past participle: 'had forgotten'.
questions.q: He ___ his wallet, so he couldn't pay.

questions.explanation: 'By the time' with a past moment takes the past perfect.
questions.q: By the time the doctor arrived, the patient ___.

questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the loss happened before she felt upset.
questions.q: She was upset because her team ___ the match.

questions.explanation: 'Had went' is wrong — the past participle of 'go' is 'gone'.
options: He had went to bed early.
He had gone to bed early.
questions.q: Which sentence is WRONG?

questions.explanation: 'Never... before' with a past reference takes the past perfect.
questions.q: I ___ never ___ such a beautiful beach before that holiday.

questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the mistake happened before she opened the letter.
questions.q: When she opened the letter, she realised she ___ a mistake.

questions.explanation: 'Never... before' in the past takes 'had never + past participle'.
options: I had never saw him before.
I have never seen him before yesterday.
I had never seen him before.
questions.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
